Audit

Does my Sdn Bhd need an audit? Exemptions in Malaysia explained

Most private companies must have their accounts audited every year — but some are exempt. Here’s how to tell which camp you’re in.

By CCM Secretarial · Updated 30 September 2026

The default rule: audit every year

Under the Companies Act 2016, a company’s financial statements must be audited by a licensed company auditor before they are circulated to members and lodged with SSM. That applies to most Sdn Bhds, whatever their size.

Who can be exempt from audit?

The Act allows exemption for certain companies. The two groups most relevant to SMEs are:

  • Dormant companies — companies that are not carrying on business and have no significant accounting transactions.
  • Threshold-qualified private companies — small private companies that meet the statutory thresholds for revenue and other criteria set out in the Act and its regulations.

Exemption is not automatic, and the conditions can be lost when circumstances change. A company that qualified one year may not qualify the next.

Even if you’re exempt, you still have duties

  • You still need proper accounting records and financial statements approved by the directors.
  • You still must lodge your annual return and, where required, financial statements with SSM.
  • You still must file Form C with LHDN within seven months of year end.
  • Banks, investors and tenders may still ask for audited accounts.

How to decide

  1. Confirm whether the company is dormant or trading.
  2. Check revenue and other threshold conditions for the financial year.
  3. Consider whether lenders, investors or clients will want audited figures anyway.
  4. Document the decision in your directors’ records.

FAQ

Quick answers

Is an audit required if my company has no revenue?

Zero-revenue or dormant companies may qualify for exemption under the Companies Act 2016, subject to the conditions. Check before you decide not to audit.

Who signs off the audited accounts?

A licensed company auditor signs the auditor’s report, and the directors approve and sign the financial statements.
